findings.title: Sign-in throttle is check-then-act: parallel guesses all pass loginWait before any failure is recorded

A half-supplied TLS pair (only tls.key or only tls.crt) is overwritten by a generated pair: deliberate in code and pinned by a test, but docs/deployment.md:154 says a pair is generated only 'With neither'
Backup directory check cannot tell an unmounted /backup: scheduled backups silently land in the container layer
A full throttle table refuses every legitimate sign-in, and the table is filled by attacker-chosen usernames
findings.notes: 2026-11-11: Documented fail-closed design; attack needs ~170-1,000 client /64s because each address is also blocked after 5 failures. Follow-up question from the user on client-IP correctness in container deployments recorded under CR-0004 (see notes in plan).

findings.title: Hasher concurrency is runtime.NumCPU(), so a burst of sign-ins can take every CPU, contrary to its stated purpose
Import that fails after an earlier section was written answers a bare 500, so the admin cannot tell what was applied
A session created after a concurrent revocation (password reset, demotion, deletion) survives it; for a deleted user /solAdmin loops
SEMP relay forwards If-None-Match/If-Match but turns the broker's 304 into a 502 upstream_unavailable
Shutdown ignores hijacked SMF/Direct WebSockets, waits on the backup loop with no deadline, and ignores a second signal
findings.notes: 2026-11-11: Process exit tears the hijacked sockets down the same way on the wire; the backup wait only stalls on a hung mount; second-signal handling not needed. Accepted.

findings.title: Store, key, backup and TLS writes are not crash-durable: no directory fsync after rename or create; writePEM ignores Close and never syncs
Generated self-signed certificate expires after 365 days and is never renewed or warned about
A missing app bundle starts the gateway anyway and serves 404s, and serveIndex logs nothing
Import merge reads the stores outside their lock, so a concurrent admin edit before replaceUsers/replaceConnections is lost
Concurrent schedule saves can leave the in-memory schedule different from backup.yaml
solace-client: a connect() on a client with a session lets the old session's DISCONNECTED handler dispose the new session
The VPN-switch flow is implemented twice and the managed copy has already drifted from the documented navigation contract
The production SEMP client contains a hard-coded demo branch that rejects any host containing 'untrust.com'
docs/architecture.md (and matching code comments) describe mechanisms the code no longer has
Core keeps runtime-written module-level singletons (hosted mode, queue-picker cache/state) instead of AppContext state
Module CSS selection is a hand-kept list separate from the variant manifests; the kitchen-sink build ships the admin modules unstyled
The variant manifest is parsed by a regex stricter than TypeScript; an unquoted module id compiles but is never bundled
Docs instruct operators to set CONN_MODES=managed, a value the gateway rejects at startup
Provisioned broker connections are hard-wired to TLS (https SEMP, wss SMF), but the connection record and the docs never say so
SSL_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY is parsed leniently while HOSTED and LOG_LEVEL are strict; a typo is silently ignored
AppContext.config is an untyped, unused field sourced from a global that nothing sets
The SSL_CERT_FILE name collides with Go's own trust-store variable, so 'env var ignored, config.yaml wins' is not true for it
Live vs restart-only config keys are two independent hand lists with no check that every key is in one of them

Kernel.sempFetch encodes Basic auth differently from the semp-client probe (a second SEMP client): non-Latin-1 credentials throw, Latin-1 ones change bytes after connect, and its 401 teardown bypasses the connections module

Queue-browser decodes binary payloads as Latin-1 strings (SDK version10 profile): UTF-8 text is garbled, the body filter misses non-ASCII terms, and every download of a payload with bytes >= 0x80 (PDF, PNG, UTF-8 text) is corrupted
publisher.send throws synchronously on an invalid destination instead of settling { ok:false }; queue-copy then browses the whole queue and reports 'drained mid-run'
QueueBrowser-fallback verify fails any queue that takes over 10 s to browse: the bind timer is never cleared on UP
Esc closes the Confirm Queue Copy dialog without cancelling: a running copy/move continues with no visible Cancel, and an un-aborted verify can overwrite a later one
Copy engine publishes through whichever destination session exists, not the one the form names: a connect that lands after the target changed redirects the run and dodges the destination gate
SEMP and gateway requests after the connect probe have no deadline; startup awaits /hosted and /managed/me serially with the event bus held
Queue picker's fetch generation counters reset on every open, so a fetch from a closed picker writes into the next one
Move mode counts a message as moved when removeMessageFromQueue throws, and still reports 'completed'
findings.notes: 2026-11-11: The SDK's removeMessageFromQueue is a fire-and-forget client ack the broker never confirms, so a broker-side removal failure cannot be detected; accepted. Docs: user-guide note under Move that removal is a client acknowledgement the broker does not confirm and that the source queue's count should be checked afterwards.

findings.title: queue-copy `state.job` is never reset (resetTransientState is dead code), so after the first run the rbac:changed destination teardown never runs
alert() is used for user-facing errors and results, against the error-handling rule, and one message tells the user to check the console

Delete converts 64-bit guaranteed message IDs to Number before acking them; at or above 2^32 the SDK's ack encoder mangles a Number, so the ack targets a non-existent ID while the row disappears and the UI reports success
A browser that goes DOWN after UP stays registered: it holds one of the 3 binding slots and blocks re-binding the queue
matchString caches one compiled RegExp per distinct pattern with no bound
findings.notes: 2026-11-11: Accepted by the owner. The cache grows by one compiled RegExp per distinct filter string typed in a session; the growth is a few bytes per pattern, so no cap.

findings.title: net/http server errors, handler panics included, are logged at INFO and dropped at the default WARN level
User and connection changes in the admin API leave no log line naming who did it or to what, unlike settings, backups and imports
At the default WARN level the gateway logs none of its effective configuration, not even its version, and the access list is never logged at any level
WARN serves as the 'always show' audit level for routine successes, while equivalent security events stay at INFO
Gateway refusal logging differs across equivalent paths: some denials and rate limits are silent, and some error lines omit the user and client
The access log names the TCP peer instead of the resolved client, and records hijacked sockets as status 200 with 0 bytes
The documented health probe (/hosted) answers 200 while the app bundle cannot be served, and a missing index file returns 404 without a log line
The sign-in and unauthenticated-request throttles fail closed silently when their tracking tables are full
Failed SEMP list calls drop the HTTP status and the gateway's error code, and non-OK SEMP responses are rendered four different ways
SDK error text bypasses solaceErrorText in the queue browser and in parts of queue-copy and the publisher
Error and warning toasts disappear after the 1-second default, and for several failures the toast is the only signal
findings.notes: 2026-11-11: Keep the 1 s toast default; the notification panel (NEW-3) keeps every toast, which is the persistent signal. Accepted.

findings.title: Several failure paths swallow the cause without a developer log, or fall back silently
Open-in-Browser and VPN-switch timeouts end with no signal to the user
Bulk delete reports a partial failure as full success, and its failure text sends the user to the console
Browser log lines have no consistent module tag and often omit the broker, VPN or queue they concern
queue-browser's forward modal reaches the DOM through document.getElementById instead of its container, because the module keeps module-scoped singletons
Dead production code: an unused config module, a probe only tests call, an unused cap constant and unreachable branches
Commented-out defensive guards from the 2026-05-26 audit are still in three services
Admin list plumbing is copy-pasted between connection-management and user-management, and setError exists six times
Protocol limits and connection defaults are repeated as literals in several places
Comments point at files, lines or siblings that no longer exist
No linter or formatter is configured or gated, and the .js modules are not type-checked
Redundant !important declarations on hover rules and module-only selectors kept in the shared stylesheet
The 100% web coverage thresholds are never enforced by CI or the tag pipeline; only a local `cov` run checks them
The Go race detector is never run, so the gateway's only race test asserts nothing
Verify and copy are never tested with createQueueBrowser throwing; the call is unguarded and the modal drops the rejection
The copy/move engine is never run against a realistic SDK (neither the demo broker nor the real SDK); its tests hand-drive mock handlers
The global fetch mock keeps its implementation and unconsumed *Once values across tests; setup.ts re-installs every other global but this one
resetQueueBrowserState() misses runtime-added state fields, and ui-forward.test.ts hand-resets instead of calling it
The gateway contract pins only refusals and admin CRUD: no successful relay, no 429/5xx, no sign-in, no headers
The RBAC glob conformance vector is copied by hand into two tables and has already drifted
routes.test.ts completeness check keys on the first path segment, so new routes under an existing segment need no row
Two shipped code sets are outside any coverage measurement: the demo tree (Release bundles) and the gate scripts
docs-links test fails on a fresh checkout because docs/improvement-plan.md is git-ignored, so the next tag's gates go red on both runners
Tag format is never validated: any v* tag (pre-release or malformed) moves `latest`, is marked the Latest GitHub release and redeploys Pages; the no-tags guard can never fire
SCA workflow calls a reusable workflow at mutable `@main`, handing it FOSSA_API_KEY and broad top-level write and OIDC permissions; runner is ubuntu-latest
findings.notes: 2026-11-11: Accept the org decision to track the reusable SCA workflow by branch (commit bb300f7, org ticket): mark accepted in docs/review/findings.json with that note; correct docs/git.md:194 to state the exception; pin the update_manifest runner to ubuntu-24.04; scope the top-level permissions to the sca_scan job.

findings.title: Compose posture tests do not forbid every widening token, let extra security_opt entries through, and leave the e2e `gateway` service unpinned
README and deployment.md quick starts give operators commands that fail or skip a required step (no SMU_VERSION, wrong file path, no backup dir, `:latest`)
Release artifacts are rebuilt in each stage instead of promoted; the image's own index.html and provisioned.html never pass check:bundles
Dockerfile base images and syntax frontend are pinned by tag, not digest
Every compose file uses the deprecated `no-new-privileges:true` colon form instead of `no-new-privileges=true`
vite-build.mjs exits 0 when vite is killed by a signal, and emptyOutDir:false keeps a stale bundle for check:bundles to pass on
The `vet` gate type-checks src/**/*.ts only: tests/, vite/vitest configs and the src .js files are never type-checked, so test fixtures typed as production types drift silently

dev.ps1 buffers each command's output until it exits and validates task names with wildcard-tolerant, case-insensitive Get-Command -- both prescribed by the dev-script contract, so a cancelled Windows run can lose its log and `dev.ps1 b*` passes the upfront check
setup.sh is an unreferenced, unhardened script that downloads an unpinned SDK with no checksum and reports success even when nothing was extracted
findings.notes: 2026-11-11: User: ignore. setup.sh stays as is; recorded as accepted.

findings.title: Per-machine graphify artifacts and a stale nested graph are tracked in git
Stale developer docs: contributing.md describes Go build-tag test variants that no longer exist; developer-guide.md says priority is set in src/registry.ts
test-report.md's 'Current files in the test tree' list is stale after the backup, icons, download and access-test suites were added
Test titles and comments cite improvement-plan item IDs and plan scenario numbers (COV-5/6/10/11/12, scenario #n)
`any` used outside the Solace SDK boundary in core (managed-semp-filter, event-bus, queue-picker, semp-discovery, semp-client)

DOMParser try/catch: ignored in parse.ts, but service-verify's copies are kept green by impossible throwing-parser stubs

Dead fallbacks and presence guards on stored-message fields that ingest always sets
Kept ignores carry stale or inaccurate justification text
